column3: “I will cut off your arm” is rendered “I will break your strength.”
The Hebrew reads “you will look at the distress of a dwelling in all that He will do good”; NASB renders “in spite of all that I do good.” The meaning is uncertain.
NASB supplies “from weeping”; “they will die as men” is rendered “will die in the prime of life.”
“A sure house” is rendered “an enduring house,” and “all the days” as “always.”
“A payment of silver” is rendered “a piece of silver,” and NASB uses “or” for “and” between silver and bread.
